name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTION_AND_MOVEMENT_MCQ_Q01 - Types of movement and muscle classification

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements regarding movement and muscular tissue in humans:

Statement I: Macrophages and leucocytes in blood exhibit amoeboid movement effected by pseudopodia and cytoskeletal microfilaments.

Statement II: Ciliary movement in the trachea helps remove dust particles, and ciliary movement also facilitates the passage of ova through the female reproductive tract.

Statement III: Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa and maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges.

Statement IV: Muscle is a specialised tissue of mesodermal origin contributing about 40–50 per cent of adult human body weight.

Statement V: Visceral muscles located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs are striated and under voluntary nervous control.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Living cells exhibit amoeboid, ciliary, flagellar, and muscular movements, while human muscular tissues are classified into skeletal, visceral, and cardiac muscles based on location, appearance, and regulation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Propositions
Macrophages and leucocytes exhibit amoeboid movement via pseudopodia formed by protoplasmic streaming and microfilaments, which is accurate. Ciliated epithelium in the trachea clears dust particles and in the female reproductive tract facilitates ova passage, which is accurate. Flagellar movement drives swimming of spermatozoa and maintains water currents in the canal system of sponges, which is accurate. Muscle tissue is of mesodermal origin and contributes 40–50 per cent of adult human body weight, which is also accurate. However, visceral (smooth) muscles lack striations and are involuntary, not striated or voluntary.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Four of the five biological propositions—covering amoeboid movement in blood cells, ciliary movement in the trachea and reproductive tract, flagellar movement in spermatozoa and sponges, and the mesodermal origin and body weight contribution of muscle—are correct, while the claim that visceral muscles are striated and voluntary is incorrect.

answer.text: Four statements are correct (I, II, III, and IV)
Three statements are correct (I, II, and III)
Four statements are correct (II, III, IV, and V)
All five statements are correct (I, II, III, IV, and V)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTION_AND_MOVEMENT_MCQ_Q02 - Skeletal muscle structure and contractile proteins

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following five statements regarding skeletal muscle ultrastructure and contractile proteins:

Statement I: Muscle bundles (fascicles) are held together by a common collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia.

Statement II: A muscle fibre is a syncitium containing many nuclei in the sarcoplasm, and its sarcoplasmic reticulum is the storehouse of calcium ions.

Statement III: An elastic fibre called the Z-line bisects each I-band, and the portion of myofibril between two successive Z-lines is a sarcomere.

Statement IV: Each actin filament has two helically wound F-actins, two tropomyosin filaments, and troponin that masks myosin-binding sites in the resting state.

Statement V: The light meromyosin (LMM) forms the globular head with a short arm that projects outwards as the cross arm.

Select the correct combination of statements:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Skeletal muscle organisation progresses from fascia-bound fascicles to multinucleated fibres containing sarcomeres, where thin actin and thick myosin filaments interact.

Step 2: Evaluation of Propositions
Fascicles are held together by fascia, which is accurate. A muscle fibre is a multinucleated syncitium whose sarcoplasmic reticulum stores \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) ions, which is accurate. The elastic Z-line bisects each I-band, and the segment between two successive Z-lines forms the functional unit called a sarcomere, which is accurate. Thin filaments comprise two helically wound F-actins (polymers of G-actin), two tropomyosin strands, and troponin distributed at regular intervals that masks myosin-binding sites at rest, which is accurate. However, it is heavy meromyosin (HMM)—not light meromyosin (LMM)—that forms the globular head and short arm projecting outwards as the cross arm.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The propositions describing fascia, syncitial muscle fibres with calcium-storing sarcoplasmic reticulum, Z-line and sarcomere boundaries, and thin-filament protein organisation are correct, whereas attributing the cross arm to LMM instead of HMM is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and V only
Statements II, III, IV, and V only
Statements I, II, III, and IV only
All five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTION_AND_MOVEMENT_MCQ_Q03 - Muscle contraction mechanism and fibre metabolism

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the mechanism of muscle contraction and muscle fibre types:

Statement I: A motor neuron and the muscle fibres connected to it form a motor unit, and acetylcholine released at the neuromuscular junction generates a sarcolemmal action potential.

Statement II: Released \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) binds to a subunit of troponin on actin filaments to unmask active sites for myosin binding.

Statement III: During contraction, the I-bands get reduced while the A-bands retain their length.

Statement IV: Binding of a new ATP breaks the cross bridge, and pumping \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) back to the sarcoplasmic cisternae causes relaxation.

Statement V: Red fibres contain very little myoglobin and few mitochondria, relying mainly on anaerobic glycolysis for ATP.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Muscle contraction follows the sliding filament mechanism initiated by acetylcholine at the motor-end plate, regulated by \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\)-troponin binding and ATP cycling, with Red and White fibres differing in aerobic capacity.

Step 2: Evaluation of Propositions
A motor neuron plus its innervated muscle fibres forms a motor unit, and acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction triggers a sarcolemmal action potential, which is accurate. Sarcoplasmic \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) binds to a troponin subunit on actin filaments, removing masking of myosin-binding sites, which is accurate. During sliding, I-bands shorten whereas A-bands maintain constant length, which is accurate. A new ATP binding to myosin breaks the cross bridge, and active return of \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) to the sarcoplasmic cisternae re-masks actin and restores Z-lines to relaxation, which is accurate. However, Red fibres possess high myoglobin content and plenty of mitochondria for aerobic ATP production; it is White fibres that have very less myoglobin and few mitochondria and depend on anaerobic processes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The propositions covering motor units and acetylcholine, \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\)-troponin unmasking, I-band shortening with constant A-band length, and ATP-driven cross-bridge breakage with \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) reuptake are correct, while the description of Red fibres as myoglobin-poor and anaerobic is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and V only
Statements I, II, III, and IV only
Statements I, III, IV, and V only
All five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTION_AND_MOVEMENT_MCQ_Q04 - Axial and appendicular skeletal bone counts

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements regarding the human axial and appendicular skeleton:

Statement I: The axial skeleton comprises 80 bones, including the skull, vertebral column, sternum, and ribs.

Statement II: The skull contains 8 cranial bones, 14 facial elements, a single hyoid bone, and 3 ear ossicles in each middle ear, and articulates via two occipital condyles.

Statement III: The vertebral column has 26 serially arranged vertebrae, with 7 cervical vertebrae present in almost all mammals including humans.

Statement IV: Of the 12 pairs of bicephalic ribs, the 1st–7th pairs are true ribs, the 8th–10th pairs are vertebrochondral (false) ribs, and the 11th–12th pairs are floating ribs.

Statement V: Each hindlimb is made of 30 bones including 8 tarsals, 5 metatarsals, and 13 phalanges.

Select the correct option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The 206 bones of the human skeleton are divided into the axial skeleton (80 bones) and the appendicular skeleton (126 bones, including 30 bones in each limb).

Step 2: Evaluation of Propositions
The axial skeleton comprises 80 bones (skull, vertebral column, sternum, ribs), which is accurate. The skull consists of 8 cranial and 14 facial bones (total 22), a single U-shaped hyoid, and 3 ear ossicles per middle ear, articulating with the atlas via two occipital condyles (dicondylic), which is accurate. The vertebral column is formed by 26 vertebrae including 7 cervical vertebrae, which is accurate. The 12 pairs of bicephalic ribs are accurately grouped into true ribs (1st–7th), vertebrochondral false ribs (8th–10th joining the 7th rib), and floating ribs (11th–12th). However, each hindlimb has 7 tarsals and 14 phalanges (\(1\text{ femur} + 1\text{ patella} + 1\text{ tibia} + 1\text{ fibula} + 7\text{ tarsals} + 5\text{ metatarsals} + 14\text{ phalanges} = 30\)), not 8 tarsals and 13 phalanges.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The propositions covering the 80-bone axial skeleton, skull and dicondylic condyles, 26-unit vertebral column with 7 cervical vertebrae, and 12 pairs of ribs are correct, whereas the claim of 8 tarsals and 13 phalanges in the hindlimb is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and V only
Statements II, III, IV, and V only
All five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V)
Statements I, II, III, and IV only

questiontext.text:
Assess the following five statements regarding girdles, joints, and disorders of the muscular and skeletal system:

Statement I: The glenoid cavity of the scapula articulates with the head of the humerus, whereas the acetabulum of the coxal bone articulates with the femur.

Statement II: Flat skull bones form immovable fibrous joints called sutures, whereas adjacent vertebrae form cartilaginous joints permitting limited movement.

Statement III: The joint between the atlas and axis is a pivot joint, and the joint between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb is a saddle joint.

Statement IV: The two halves of the pelvic girdle meet ventrally to form the pubic symphysis containing fibrous cartilage.

Statement V: Osteoporosis is commonly caused by elevated estrogen levels, and tetany results from high \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) levels in body fluid.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Limb articulation relies on specific girdle cavities and synovial joints, while fibrous and cartilaginous joints provide stability and limited mobility, and hormonal or ionic imbalances cause skeletal-muscular disorders.

Step 2: Evaluation of Propositions
The glenoid cavity below the scapular acromion articulates with the head of the humerus, and the acetabulum formed by fusion of ilium, ischium, and pubis articulates with the femur; this is accurate. Flat skull bones fuse end-to-end via dense fibrous connective tissue as immovable sutures, while adjacent vertebrae form cartilaginous joints allowing limited movement; this is accurate. The atlas–axis joint is a synovial pivot joint, and the carpal–metacarpal joint of the thumb is a synovial saddle joint; this is accurate. The two pelvic halves meet ventrally at the pubic symphysis containing fibrous cartilage; this is accurate. However, osteoporosis is commonly associated with decreased (not elevated) estrogen levels, and tetany is caused by low (not high) \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) levels in body fluid.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The propositions covering girdle-limb articulations, fibrous sutures and cartilaginous intervertebral joints, pivot and saddle synovial joints, and the fibrous-cartilage pubic symphysis are correct, whereas the claims linking osteoporosis to elevated estrogen and tetany to high \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) are incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and IV only
Statements I, II, III, and V only
Statements II, III, IV, and V only
All five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V)
